sentences.zh: 而是说：嘿，我两周后要举办一个晚宴。

sentences.en: I'd love to see you guys.
sentences.zh: 我很希望能见到你们。

sentences.en: Or, hey, I would love to go for a walk this week.
sentences.zh: 或者：嘿，这周我很想去散散步。

sentences.en: And, you know, are you around on Saturday?
sentences.zh: 你周六有空吗？

sentences.en: And so that's within your control, what you do or don't do.
sentences.zh: 所以这些都在你的掌控之中，即你做什么或不做什么。

sentences.en: And then the final thing is, is the third thing that's in your control is how you respond to the emotions that rise up.
sentences.zh: 最后一点，也是第三件你所能掌控的事，就是你如何回应内心升起的情绪。

sentences.en: Because the emotions are valid.
sentences.zh: 因为这些情绪是合理的。

sentences.en: It is a sign that you're normal if you're hurt, if somebody doesn't include you.
sentences.zh: 如果有人没带上你，你感到受伤，这说明你很正常。

sentences.en: But you get to choose whether or not those normal emotions run you over or whether or not you let them rise and fall and then you choose how to respond.
sentences.zh: 但你可以选择是让这些正常的情绪压垮你，还是让它们自然起伏，然后由你来决定如何回应。

sentences.en: Is that where the, is that where the, I'm like still thinking about this word you used, which is superiority, because generally there's like a negative valence to that, right?
sentences.zh: 这就是……我还在思考你用的那个词，即“优越感”，因为通常这个词带有负面色彩，对吧？

sentences.en: But I'm, I'm trying to understand yours is not so much like a superiority over others or like a negative interpretation of it.
sentences.zh: 但我正试图理解，你所说的并不是对他人的优越感，也不是负面的解读。

sentences.en: Can you explain that piece of the let them theory a bit more?
sentences.zh: 你能再多解释一下“随他们去”理论中的那一部分吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 可以。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: It's superiority over your own emotional response to what's happening.
sentences.zh: 那是对你自身情绪反应的优越感，即对所发生之事的反应。

sentences.en: That's what I was, yeah.
sentences.zh: 我刚才想说的就是这个，没错。

sentences.en: See, not, we're all, we're all basically eight-year-old children.
sentences.zh: 你看，我们本质上都是八岁的孩子。

sentences.en: Every single adult that you meet and that you deal with every day is an eight-year-old in a big body.
sentences.zh: 你每天遇到的每一个成年人，其实都是装在成年躯壳里的八岁小孩。

sentences.en: None of us know how to manage our emotions because that is a skill that you have to want to learn
sentences.zh: 我们都没学会如何管理自己的情绪，因为那是一项你需要主动去学习的技能，

sentences.en: and you have to practice it because people are really annoying and life is really stressful.
sentences.zh: 而且你必须去实践它，因为人们真的很烦人，生活也压力重重。

sentences.en: But that doesn't mean you have to allow other people's opinions, moods, expectations, and beliefs to drain your time and energy.
sentences.zh: 但这并不意味着你必须允许他人的观点、情绪、期望和信念来消耗你的时间和精力。

sentences.en: And when you then say, let me, you then take the power back.
sentences.zh: 当你对自己说“随他们去”时，你就夺回了掌控权。

sentences.en: And you cue yourself to say, let me choose if this is worth worrying about.
sentences.zh: 你是在提醒自己：让我来选择这是否值得我担心。

sentences.en: Let me choose if this is a conversation I want to engage in.
sentences.zh: 让我来选择这是否是我想要参与的对话。

sentences.en: Let me choose whether or not I'm going to spend seven hours reading the headlines and feeling freaked out and powerless or if I'm going to take all that power back and go focus on
sentences.zh: 让我来选择是否要花七个小时去读新闻标题，让自己感到惊慌和无力，还是夺回掌控权，专注于

sentences.en: making the changes happen that I want to see that I'm worried about in this world or in my family or in my community.
sentences.zh: 去实现我想要看到的改变，那些我为之担忧的世界、家庭或社区层面的改变。

sentences.en: And it was a huge wake-up call for me to realize how much power I had been unknowingly giving
sentences.zh: 意识到我曾无意中将多少力量交给了

sentences.en: to other people's opinions, to their behavior, to their rudeness, to their moods, to all that stuff.
sentences.zh: 他人的观点、行为、粗鲁、情绪以及所有这些琐事，这对我来说是一个巨大的警钟。

sentences.en: I kind of hate this word, but as like a true control freak, it is deeply tough, right, to like loosen the vice grip of my idea of control, my impulse to control.
sentences.zh: 我有点讨厌这个词，但作为一个真正的控制狂，想要松开我对控制的执念和冲动，真的非常困难，对吧？

sentences.en: I guess I wonder, like, where do you land?
sentences.zh: 我猜我在想，你处于什么位置？

sentences.en: Are you a similar kind of control freak?
sentences.zh: 你也是那种控制狂吗？

sentences.en: And if so, I kind of know the answer to that one.
sentences.zh: 如果真是这样，我大概知道答案了。

sentences.en: I can't believe you even have to ask that question.
sentences.zh: 真不敢相信你竟然还要问这个问题。

sentences.en: I know, I know, I know.
sentences.zh: 我知道，我知道，我知道。

sentences.en: You know, you've got to pose the question.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你总得把问题提出来。

sentences.en: Where do you think that impulse comes from in you?
sentences.zh: 你觉得你这种冲动源于哪里？

sentences.en: Well, I know where it comes from.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我知道它源于哪里。

sentences.en: And by the way, everybody's a control freak.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，每个人都是控制狂。

sentences.en: The range is how we express it on the outside.
sentences.zh: 区别在于我们如何在外在表现出来。

sentences.en: Huh, yeah.
sentences.zh: 哈，是的。

sentences.en: And here's the good news.
sentences.zh: 好消息是：

sentences.en: The let them theory isn't going to force you to stop controlling things.
sentences.zh: “随他们去”理论并不会强迫你停止控制一切。

sentences.en: The let them theory teaches you what you can control.
sentences.zh: “随他们去”理论教你的是你能控制什么。

sentences.en: So it makes you way more effective at how you use your time and energy and how you direct
sentences.zh: 所以它让你在利用时间和精力方面变得高效得多，让你能将精力集中

sentences.en: it at what's actually in your control instead of burning through your time and energy trying to change and manage other people.
sentences.zh: 在真正可控的事情上，而不是浪费时间和精力去试图改变和管理他人。

sentences.en: And so, yes, I'm a control freak.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，我是个控制狂。

sentences.en: I'm also married to a Buddhist, which is super annoying because he's like very chill.
sentences.zh: 我还嫁给了一个佛教徒，这真的很烦人，因为他总是非常淡定。

sentences.en: And I have been studying stoicism.
sentences.zh: 我一直在研究斯多葛学派。

sentences.en: I've been trying to stop gripping the wheel of life.
sentences.zh: 我一直在努力停止紧握生活的方向盘。

sentences.en: But the bottom line is, is that every human being has a fundamental hardwired need for control, which is not going anywhere.
sentences.zh: 但底线是，每个人都有对控制的根本性、与生俱来的需求，这是无法消除的。

sentences.en: Anna, if you do something that really upsets me, your behavior now makes me feel out of control.
sentences.zh: 安娜，如果你做了让我非常心烦的事，你的行为现在让我感到失控。

sentences.en: And the mistake that I made for 54 years, and this is automatic wiring, is because your behavior,
sentences.zh: 而我54年来所犯的错误——这是自动化的本能反应——是因为你的行为，

sentences.en: Anna's not motivated enough in school.
sentences.zh: 比如安娜在学校不够努力。

sentences.en: Anna's not texting me back when I think she should.
sentences.zh: 安娜没有在我认为她应该回复的时候给我发短信。

sentences.en: Anna's not working hard enough at her job.
sentences.zh: 安娜在工作上不够努力。

sentences.en: Anna's not hearing what I think she should eat.
sentences.zh: 安娜没有听从我关于她该吃什么的建议。

sentences.en: Yeah, Anna's wearing the wrong thing to this, that, and the other thing.
sentences.zh: 是的，安娜在穿衣打扮上出了错，诸如此类。

sentences.en: But Anna's behavior is now bothering me, so I feel out of control.
sentences.zh: 但安娜的行为现在困扰着我，所以我感到失控。

sentences.en: And then I, and everybody makes a fatal mistake.
sentences.zh: 然后我，每个人都会犯一个致命的错误。

sentences.en: I actually cross a line, and I try to motivate or change or pressure or guilt you, or I tell you my opinion.
sentences.zh: 我越界了，我试图去激励、改变、施压或让你感到内疚，或者我强加给你我的观点。

sentences.en: And guess what?
sentences.zh: 你猜怎么着？

sentences.en: You have the same need to be in control of yourself as I have to be in control of myself.
sentences.zh: 你和我一样，都有控制自己的需求。

sentences.en: And that means the second I start telling you what to do, or I've got an opinion that you don't care about, I'm not motivating you.
sentences.zh: 这意味着当我开始告诉你该怎么做，或者表达你根本不在乎的观点时，我并不能激励你。

sentences.en: I'm actually creating resistance to change, because you're now going to fight to be in control of yourself.
sentences.zh: 我实际上是在制造改变的阻力，因为你现在会为了掌控自己而抗争。

sentences.en: There in lies, Anna, the source of all problems in every relationship, right there.
sentences.zh: 安娜，这正是所有关系中一切问题的根源所在。

sentences.en: We're not accepting each other and loving each other.
sentences.zh: 我们没有接纳彼此、爱彼此。

sentences.en: We're controlling each other.
sentences.zh: 我们在控制彼此。

sentences.en: And that's not love.
sentences.zh: 那不是爱。

sentences.en: That's judgment.
sentences.zh: 那是评判。

sentences.en: I wonder if you could share, too, a story where you felt very out of control.
sentences.zh: 我想知道你能不能分享一个你感到非常失控的故事？

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: I can give you two great examples.
sentences.zh: 我可以给你举两个很好的例子。

sentences.en: So the first one is our son, who's 20 now, when he was in kind of middle school to like right before high school.
sentences.zh: 第一个例子是关于我们的儿子，他现在20岁了，当时他大概在初中到高中之前的那段时间。

sentences.en: God, I wish I had to let them, theory.
sentences.zh: 天哪，我真希望当时就有“随他们去”理论。

sentences.en: Because he was really struggling.
sentences.zh: 因为他当时真的很挣扎。

sentences.en: We had just figured out that he had dyslexia and dysgraphia and ADHD, and he bounced from the public school to a school for language-based learning disabilities.
sentences.zh: 我们刚发现他有阅读障碍、书写障碍和多动症，他从公立学校转到了一所针对语言学习障碍的学校。

sentences.en: Then he bounced to a small private school for seventh and eighth grade.
sentences.zh: 然后他又转到了一所七、八年级的小型私立学校。

sentences.en: He was miserable.
sentences.zh: 他当时很痛苦。

sentences.en: The poor kid was so lonely.
sentences.zh: 这可怜的孩子太孤独了。

sentences.en: All of this had just taken the spark right out of him.
sentences.zh: 这一切已经让他失去了活力。

sentences.en: And he gets to high school.
sentences.zh: 然后他上了高中。

sentences.en: And, you know, it's a huge mistake that parents make.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这是父母常犯的一个巨大错误。

sentences.en: And it's thinking you know beSt.
sentences.zh: 那就是自以为是。

sentences.en: Your kids know when they're not doing well in school.
sentences.zh: 你的孩子知道他们什么时候在学校表现不好。

sentences.en: They don't need you Clydesdaling up the stairs and yelling at them because they're on the video games.
sentences.zh: 他们不需要你像克莱兹代尔马一样冲上楼，因为他们在玩游戏就对他们大吼大叫。

sentences.en: What I've come to realize, and this comes from a lot of the research in building the case for the let them theory, is that everybody wants to thrive.
sentences.zh: 我后来意识到，这来自于为“随他们去”理论建立案例时所做的大量研究，每个人都想茁壮成长。

sentences.en: Like if your kids are not doing well in school, it's not because they don't want to do well.
sentences.zh: 如果你的孩子在学校表现不好，那不是因为他们不想表现好。

sentences.en: It's not a lack of motivation.
sentences.zh: 这不是缺乏动力的问题。

sentences.en: It is either skills that are missing or worse, it's a sense of discouragement that they won't be able to do any better.
sentences.zh: 要么是缺乏技能，要么更糟，是一种觉得自己无法做得更好的挫败感。

sentences.en: And so a huge mistake that I made as a parent is thinking that you can force someone else to change or force someone else to care or motivate somebody by being Captain Obvious.
sentences.zh: 所以作为父母，我犯的一个大错就是认为你可以强迫别人改变，或者强迫别人去关心，或者通过说些显而易见的废话来激励别人。

sentences.en: So just like a lot of parents, like he would get home from school in early high school,
sentences.zh: 就像很多父母一样，他高中刚开始时放学回家，

sentences.en: and I would hear him upstairs talking to his friends playing Fortnite or whatever it was that they were playing.
sentences.zh: 我会听到他在楼上和朋友们玩《堡垒之夜》或者别的什么游戏。

sentences.en: And I'd be like, what is he doing up there?
sentences.zh: 我会想，他在楼上干什么呢？

sentences.en: And I would then stomp up the stairs, and I would fly open the door, and I'd be like, you know, dude, you got to be stuck.
sentences.zh: 然后我会跺着脚上楼，猛地推开门，说：嘿，伙计，你得学习了。

sentences.en: But you don't think he knows that in order to get better grades?
sentences.zh: 但你难道不觉得他自己知道为了取得好成绩需要学习吗？

sentences.en: So now I'm applying pressure, which is the exact opposite of what he needs.
sentences.zh: 所以我现在是在施加压力，这恰恰是他最不需要的。

sentences.en: Because here's what I want you to consider.
sentences.zh: 因为我想让你考虑一下这一点。

sentences.en: Do you know how hard it is to know that you're doing the worst of anybody?
sentences.zh: 你知道那种感觉吗？知道自己表现得比谁都差，这有多难受？

sentences.en: Do you know how much pressure that is?
sentences.zh: 你知道那压力有多大吗？

sentences.en: Don't you think that if they could snap their fingers and change this, they would?
sentences.zh: 你不觉得如果他们能打个响指就改变现状，他们早就做了吗？

sentences.en: Of course they would.
sentences.zh: 他们当然会。

sentences.en: Same thing with your friends or your family members that are struggling with their health or their weight.
sentences.zh: 你的朋友或家人在为健康或体重挣扎时也是一样。

sentences.en: You don't think they know that they need to go for a walk?
sentences.zh: 你不觉得他们知道自己需要去散散步吗？

sentences.en: And so now here you come in with the new sneakers and trying to be all, like, motivational.
sentences.zh: 所以现在你穿着新运动鞋进来了，试图表现得很有激励性。

sentences.en: It just is like, okay, yeah, I've never thought about going for a walk.
sentences.zh: 这只会让人觉得：好吧，是啊，我从没想过要去散步。

sentences.en: Thanks for the suggestion.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你的建议。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对吧。

sentences.en: It pushes someone away.
sentences.zh: 这会把人推开。

sentences.en: That's not what people need.
sentences.zh: 那不是人们所需要的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: What people need is for you to be with them.
sentences.zh: 人们需要的是你的陪伴。

sentences.en: And so when you say, let them, let him play the video games, let him do the thing that actually comes easy for him.
sentences.zh: 所以当你对自己说“随他们去”时，让他玩游戏，让他做那些对他来说容易的事。

sentences.en: That's why he's doing it.
sentences.zh: 这就是他为什么这么做的原因。

sentences.en: And then you use, this comes from Dr. Stuart Ablon with adult kids, but it works with adults too, is you take this with them approach.
sentences.zh: 然后你使用这种方法——这是斯图尔特·阿布隆博士针对成年子女提出的，但也适用于成年人——即“与他们同行”的方法。

sentences.en: You go upstairs and you have a different conversation.
sentences.zh: 你上楼去，进行一次不同的对话。

sentences.en: You say, hey, I'm really sorry.
sentences.zh: 你说：嘿，真的很抱歉。

sentences.en: I've been putting a lot of pressure on you.
sentences.zh: 我一直给你施加了太大的压力。

sentences.en: I have a lot of opinions.
sentences.zh: 我有太多的观点了。

sentences.en: That must be a pain to constantly have me nagging you.
sentences.zh: 一直被我唠叨一定很烦人。

sentences.en: I'm really sorry about that.
sentences.zh: 对此我真的很抱歉。

sentences.en: You know, I haven't bothered to ask you, how do you feel about school?
sentences.zh: 你知道，我还没问过你，你对学校有什么感觉？

sentences.en: And even if somebody's like, oh, I don't know, you're stirring up this conflict between what's actually happening and what they'd like to be happening.
sentences.zh: 即使有人说：哦，我不知道。你正在激发他们内心关于“现实情况”与“他们希望的情况”之间的冲突。

sentences.en: And that belief is what's coming to mind is like, I trust you, right?
sentences.zh: 而那个信念，浮现在我脑海中的是：我相信你，对吧？

sentences.en: I trust that you are, you know, in this case with your son, a person who is thinking and aware and trying and wants to get better.
sentences.zh: 我相信你，在这个例子中就是你的儿子，是一个有思想、有意识、在努力并想要变得更好的人。

sentences.en: And it really does remind me of the modern love essay you chose to read today, which is an incredibly high stakes, exciting, extreme sort of version of letting go of control, of
sentences.zh: 这真的让我想起了你今天选择阅读的那篇《现代爱情》文章，那是一个极高风险、令人兴奋、极端的放手控制的版本，关于

sentences.en: truSt.
sentences.zh: 信任。

sentences.en: I guess I want to, you know, before we get to it, I would love to know, considering everything we've been talking about, what drew you to this essay specifically?
sentences.zh: 我想，在进入正题之前，考虑到我们一直在谈论的一切，我很想知道是什么让你特别选择了这篇文章？

sentences.en: It's interesting, Anna, that you said these things are complicated because one of the reasons why I love the let them theory is it makes things very simple.
sentences.zh: 安娜，你说这些事情很复杂，这很有趣，因为我喜欢“随他们去”理论的原因之一，就是它让事情变得非常简单。

sentences.en: It's going to turn what you think trust is on its head.
sentences.zh: 它会颠覆你对信任的认知。

sentences.en: And because the topic of control is actually very simple.
sentences.zh: 因为关于控制的话题实际上非常简单。

sentences.en: And when you recognize that, it's very clear where your power is and where it isn't.
sentences.zh: 当你认识到这一点时，你的力量在哪里，不在哪里，就非常清楚了。

sentences.en: And it's also very clear where you have handed power to other people.
sentences.zh: 而且你把力量交给了谁，也一目了然。

sentences.en: And so one of the reasons why I picked this particular essay entitled, You Have to Let Go to Move On, is because I felt that this essay was so relatable.
sentences.zh: 所以我选择这篇题为《你必须放手才能继续前行》的文章的原因之一，是因为我觉得这篇文章太能引起共鸣了。

sentences.en: It was so honest and it was full of these subtle moments that I think anybody can find themselves
sentences.zh: 它非常诚实，充满了那些微妙的时刻，我想任何人都能在其中找到自己的影子，

sentences.en: in when it comes to the things that you really want in life and how you stop yourself from fully going after it because it feels like you don't have control.
sentences.zh: 当涉及到你生活中真正想要的东西，以及你如何因为感觉自己无法掌控而阻止自己全力以赴时。

sentences.en: After the break, Mel Robbins reads the essay, You Have to Let Go to Move On, by Jasmine Donahue.
sentences.zh: 休息之后，梅尔·罗宾斯将朗读由贾斯敏·多纳休撰写的文章《你必须放手才能继续前行》。

sentences.en: And she gives her own advice on letting go to find love.
sentences.zh: 她还会就如何放手去寻找真爱给出自己的建议。

sentences.en: Stay with us.
sentences.zh: 请留下来陪我。

sentences.en: You Have to Let Go to Move On, by Jasmine Donahue.
sentences.zh: 《必须放手才能前行》，作者：茉莉·多纳休。

sentences.en: My dating profile picture, blurry, distant figure in a desert landscape, suggested a great deal about my ambivalence, I wanted, and I didn't want.
sentences.zh: 我的约会资料照片——一张在沙漠景观中模糊不清、遥远的身影——暗示了我内心极大的矛盾：我既想要，又不想要。

sentences.en: At 47, divorced for nearly two decades and with my daughters grown, I cherished my solitude.
sentences.zh: 47岁那年，我离婚近二十年，女儿们也已长大成人，我非常享受独处的时光。

sentences.en: But sometimes, when I heard the mice rustling in the attic, I thought of the newspaper story
sentences.zh: 但有时，当我听到阁楼里老鼠窸窸窣窣的声音时，我会想起那篇报纸上的报道，

sentences.en: I'd read about a man not far from where I lived who had been found dead in his flat, partially eaten by rats.
sentences.zh: 我读过一个离我不远的人，他被发现死在公寓里，尸体被老鼠啃食了一部分。

sentences.en: Sometimes, I tired of my own company.
sentences.zh: 有时，我厌倦了独自一人的生活。

sentences.en: Occasionally, I was lonely.
sentences.zh: 偶尔，我也会感到孤独。

sentences.en: I had forgotten what it felt like to touch someone or to be touched.
sentences.zh: 我已经忘记了触碰他人或被他人触碰是什么感觉。

sentences.en: When I held my own hand in the dark to remind myself, my hand seemed small and cool, as if it belonged to someone else.
sentences.zh: 当我在黑暗中握住自己的手以提醒自己存在时，我的手显得又小又凉，仿佛属于别人。

sentences.en: I wanted connection, but I didn't want what it always seemed to coSt.
sentences.zh: 我渴望建立联结，但我不想付出它似乎总是要求的代价。

sentences.en: The men who turned me into the sole focus of their lives, you're the only thing worth living for.
sentences.zh: 那些把我当作生活唯一重心，说“你是我活下去的唯一意义”的男人。

sentences.en: The men who told me what I wanted and didn't want rather than what they wanted or didn't want.
sentences.zh: 那些告诉我我想要什么、不想要什么，而不是表达他们自己想要或不想要什么的男人。

sentences.en: The men whose expression of concern for my safety revealed itself to be a mask for control and
sentences.zh: 那些打着关心我安全的名义，实则以此作为控制和

sentences.en: coercion, whose words moved from, you shouldn't, to, you can't, as they stood blocking the door, preventing me from leaving.
sentences.zh: 胁迫手段的男人，他们站在门口挡住去路，不让我离开，话语从“你不应该”变成了“你不能”。

sentences.en: If the profile picture I chose suggested my ambivalence, then the fact that I chose Edinburgh for my location drove it home.
sentences.zh: 如果我选的照片暗示了我的矛盾，那么我选择爱丁堡作为定位，更是将这种矛盾体现得淋漓尽致。

sentences.en: Edinburgh lies two national borders and a seven-hour train journey from where I live in a rural part of Wales.
sentences.zh: 爱丁堡距离我居住的威尔士乡村有两条国界线和七小时的火车车程。

sentences.en: At the time, one of my daughters was studying at Edinburgh University, and I visited regularly.
sentences.zh: 当时，我的一个女儿在爱丁堡大学读书，我会定期去看她。

sentences.en: I was flirting with the idea of moving to Scotland, and it struck me that it might be a good idea to get to know some people there before making the decision to move.
sentences.zh: 我当时在考虑搬到苏格兰，心想在做决定之前先去了解一下那里的人或许是个好主意。

sentences.en: In reality, trying out online dating at a distance of 350 miles seemed like a good deal safer than trying it out in your home.
sentences.zh: 实际上，在350英里外尝试在线约会，似乎比在自己家附近尝试要安全得多。

sentences.en: Doing so could let me test the water without really taking a risk.
sentences.zh: 这样做可以让我试水，而无需真正承担风险。

sentences.en: And even if online dating was only a modern version of my widowed aunt matchmaking at an
sentences.zh: 即便在线约会只是我那位守寡的姑妈在18世纪谷仓舞会上做媒的现代版，

sentences.en: 18th century barn dancer ball, it seemed so artificial, so antithetical to the spontaneity and accident that creates romance, that I thought it would be safe.
sentences.zh: 它看起来如此虚假，与创造浪漫的偶然性和自发性背道而驰，以至于我觉得它是安全的。

sentences.en: There were the usual suspects, who ignored my photo and what it said about my ambivalence, the plump accountant who told me I was beautiful despite not knowing what I looked like,
sentences.zh: 当然也有一些“惯犯”，他们无视我的照片及其所暗示的矛盾心理，比如那个胖会计，在根本不知道我长什么样的情况下就说我很漂亮；

sentences.en: the purported U.S.
sentences.zh: 还有那个自称是美国

sentences.en: Marine in Iraq, who used all caps and would no doubt be sending me some scammer message about needing me to transfer money.
sentences.zh: 驻伊拉克海军陆战队的家伙，他全用大写字母发消息，毫无疑问会给我发那种让我转账的诈骗信息。

sentences.en: A slightly alarming New York banker wanted me to meet, had to meet me, and would get on a plane to come meet me the minute I replied.
sentences.zh: 还有一个令人不安的纽约银行家，他非要见我，一定要见我，只要我回复，他就会立刻坐飞机来见我。

sentences.en: I looked at the profile of a man at sea.
sentences.zh: 我看了看一个海上工作男人的资料。

sentences.en: He seemed safely distant.
sentences.zh: 他看起来距离很远，很安全。

sentences.en: And there was a climber with a kind face who was good at chopping wood.
sentences.zh: 还有一个面相和善、擅长劈柴的登山者。

sentences.en: He lived in Carlisle, a five-hour drive away.
sentences.zh: 他住在卡莱尔，开车要五个小时。

sentences.en: I'm fair with an axe, but terrified of heights, so he seemed safe too.
sentences.zh: 我用斧头还行，但有恐高症，所以他看起来也很安全。

sentences.en: I didn't answer the accountant or the marine or the banker, and the man at sea didn't reply to me.
sentences.zh: 我没有回复那个会计、海军陆战队员或银行家，而那个海上工作的男人也没有回复我。

sentences.en: But the climber did.
sentences.zh: 但那个登山者回复了。

sentences.en: Soon, we were writing to each other, regularly, across the shortening days of early autumn.
sentences.zh: 很快，我们开始在初秋渐短的白昼里频繁通信。

sentences.en: Our correspondence reminded me of having a pen pal.
sentences.zh: 我们的通信让我想起了笔友。

sentences.en: We told each other little details of our day-to-day lives, of things we had seen or done.
sentences.zh: 我们向对方讲述日常生活中琐碎的细节，分享我们所见所做的事。

sentences.en: But we never mentioned meeting.
sentences.zh: 但我们从未提过见面。

sentences.en: I asked him about climbing, but I really didn't want to know.
sentences.zh: 我问过他关于登山的事，但我其实并不想知道。

sentences.en: Now, I experienced vertigo at the top of a flight of stairs, and the pictures of him inching along a crag above a hundred-foot drop gave me palpitations.
sentences.zh: 现在，我在楼梯顶端都会感到眩晕，而他沿着百英尺落差的岩壁缓慢移动的照片让我心悸。

sentences.en: Even if we were to meet, I knew we wouldn't get beyond that first coffee in a cafe, or his preference, a pint of real ale in a pub.
sentences.zh: 即使我们见面了，我也知道我们顶多只能一起喝杯咖啡，或者按他的喜好，去酒吧喝杯精酿啤酒。

sentences.en: Ten months later, I'm stepping up to the foot of a crag.
sentences.zh: 十个月后，我正站在岩壁脚下。

sentences.en: Everything has left my mind but fear.
sentences.zh: 我脑子里除了恐惧，什么都没有了。

sentences.en: In my peripheral vision, a nightmare of nothingness.
sentences.zh: 余光中，是一片虚无的梦魇。

sentences.en: Beneath me, a black slab descends steeply to a limpet-crusted causeway of broken columns.
sentences.zh: 在我下方，一块黑色岩板陡峭地延伸向布满藤壶的破碎石柱堤道。

sentences.en: I tamp down the fear, but halfway up this sea stack of the Coast of Mall, I lose control of it, and I get stuck.
sentences.zh: 我强压恐惧，但在爬到马尔海岸这座海蚀柱一半高度时，我失去了控制，被困住了。

sentences.en: My feet are wedged into a vertical crack.
sentences.zh: 我的双脚卡在一条垂直的裂缝里。

sentences.en: There's a foothold to my left, a bit higher up, but my left foot is pinned beneath my right, and I can't move.
sentences.zh: 左上方有一处落脚点，但我的左脚被右脚压在下面，动弹不得。

sentences.en: I can't move my right foot either.
sentences.zh: 我的右脚也动不了。

sentences.en: There's nowhere else to place it.
sentences.zh: 没有其他地方可以落脚了。

sentences.en: I can't shift my weight, so I might free my left foot, and I can't step back down because that way is the void, the nothingness.
sentences.zh: 我无法转移重心来解放左脚，也无法退回去，因为下面就是虚空，就是那片虚无。

sentences.en: I'm stuck, and I cannot see a way that I can ever move.
sentences.zh: 我被困住了，看不到任何脱身的办法。

sentences.en: My brain toys with me, tells me it's insoluble.
sentences.zh: 我的大脑在戏弄我，告诉我这是死局。

sentences.en: Even supposing my right foot finds a foothold beneath me, where can I put my left foot but back in this crack?
sentences.zh: 就算假设我的右脚能在下方找到落脚点，我的左脚除了放回这个裂缝里还能放哪儿呢？

sentences.en: My feet do a little dance in the crack, but only end up wedged in more tightly.
sentences.zh: 我的双脚在裂缝里挣扎，结果却卡得更紧了。

sentences.en: I've got you, he calls down from above, out of sight.
sentences.zh: “我抓住你了，”他在上方喊道，我看不到他。

sentences.en: You're safe.
sentences.zh: “你是安全的。”

sentences.en: He has me secured by a rope, but his words just sound like meaningless noise.
sentences.zh: 他用绳子固定着我，但他的话听起来就像毫无意义的噪音。

sentences.en: My heart races.
sentences.zh: 我的心跳加速。

sentences.en: I can't breathe.
sentences.zh: 我无法呼吸。

sentences.en: I have only the jangled sense of catastrophe.
sentences.zh: 我只感到一阵混乱的灾难感。

sentences.en: He takes in the rope a little, so that I can feel he's there at the other end holding me.
sentences.zh: 他收紧了一点绳子，让我能感觉到他在另一端支撑着我。

sentences.en: But I'm frozen, panicking.
sentences.zh: 但我僵住了，陷入了恐慌。

sentences.en: My hands grip the rock convulsively, and my left leg begins to cramp.
sentences.zh: 我的双手痉挛般地抓紧岩石，左腿开始抽筋。

sentences.en: Somehow, though, remembering being in labor, I get my breathing under control.
sentences.zh: 不知怎的，我想起分娩时的经历，终于控制住了呼吸。

sentences.en: My heart slows from its mad race to a fast, painful pounding.
sentences.zh: 心跳从疯狂的疾驰慢了下来，变成了快速而痛苦的跳动。

sentences.en: I tell the disembodied voice above me to shut up, stop making noise.
sentences.zh: 我让上方那个看不见的声音闭嘴，别再制造噪音。

sentences.en: Anyways, I swear out loud that if I ever get out of this, I will never, ever do it again.
sentences.zh: 总之，我大声发誓，如果我能活着出去，我再也不会做这种事了。

sentences.en: I jiggle my feet, lodging my right foot a little higher in the crack, and I manage to slip my left foot out from underneath it.
sentences.zh: 我晃动双脚，把右脚在裂缝里往上挪了一点，终于设法把左脚从下面抽了出来。

sentences.en: Then I jam it in somehow, scabbling and slipping as I bring my right foot back down and in under
sentences.zh: 然后我设法把它塞进去，在把右脚向下移到左脚下方时，我抓挠着、滑落着，

sentences.en: the left, my left foot is free to move, but now I have to lunge upward to get it onto the foothold to the left, and that means letting go of what I'm gripping so tightly.
sentences.zh: 左脚终于可以自由活动了，但现在我必须奋力向上跃起才能把它踩到左边的落脚点上，这意味着我必须松开紧紧抓着的东西。

sentences.en: I don't know what I'll be able to grab hold of higher up when I lunge.
sentences.zh: 我不知道跃起后上面能抓到什么。

sentences.en: I can't let go, and I know I have to let go to be able to move on.
sentences.zh: 我不敢松手，但我知道必须放手才能前行。

sentences.en: And this seems both a profound truth, and at the same time, the most trite and redundant thought I've ever had.
sentences.zh: 这看起来既是一个深刻的真理，同时又是我所想过的最陈腐、最冗余的念头。

sentences.en: I mean, this isn't some personal growth seminar.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这又不是什么个人成长研讨会。

sentences.en: I think enraged at myself.
sentences.zh: 我愤怒地对自己想道。

sentences.en: This is a disaster.
sentences.zh: 这简直是一场灾难。

sentences.en: And then, because in the end I have to, though I might have nothing to hold onto, I launch myself into the unknown.
sentences.zh: 然后，因为最终我必须这样做，尽管可能无处可抓，我还是把自己抛向了未知。

sentences.en: Miraculously, my left hand finds a great lumpy protrusion.
sentences.zh: 奇迹般地，我的左手摸到了一块巨大的凸起。

sentences.en: And then there's a hold from my right, and suddenly, everything is possible.
sentences.zh: 接着右手也找到了支撑点，突然间，一切皆有可能。

sentences.en: The rest has its own logic, almost as though the handholds and footholds appear as I need them, a known thing before it's known.
sentences.zh: 剩下的过程有它自己的逻辑，仿佛手脚落点在我需要时就会出现，在被感知之前就已经存在。

sentences.en: And with a kind of exquisite economy, I'm lifting myself from one hold to the next, and
sentences.zh: 带着一种精妙的省力感，我从一个支撑点移向下一个，

sentences.en: I'm at the lip, and at the top, and there he is, the man who all along has been keeping me safe, whose voice has been carrying me, even though I told him to shut up, while I
sentences.zh: 我到了边缘，到了顶端，他就在那里，那个一直保护着我、用声音支撑着我的人，尽管我让他闭嘴，而我

sentences.en: took the time to find my way and keep going.
sentences.zh: 花时间找到了自己的路并继续前行。

sentences.en: Trust, I say.
sentences.zh: “信任，”我说。

sentences.en: Gabbling in the release of endorphins and in a delirium lying on my back on the wide, flat rock.
sentences.zh: 内啡肽释放带来的快感让我语无伦次，我躺在宽阔平坦的岩石上，处于一种谵妄状态。

sentences.en: TruSt.
sentences.zh: “信任。”

sentences.en: It's all about truSt.
sentences.zh: 一切都在于信任。

sentences.en: I watch him, this man who's not afraid of being afraid, who does not need to keep me from taking risks.
sentences.zh: 我看着他，这个不怕恐惧、不需要阻止我冒险的男人。

sentences.en: I watch him coiling the rope with which he kept me safe, shaking his head resignedly over the slimy puddle of guano he landed it in.
sentences.zh: 我看着他收起那根保护我的绳子，无奈地摇着头，看着绳子落入的那滩黏糊糊的鸟粪。

sentences.en: And I realize that, remarkably, he trusted me too.
sentences.zh: 我意识到，令人惊奇的是，他也信任我。

sentences.en: He placed his trust in me to keep him safe as he climbed first, even though I hardly knew what I was doing.
sentences.zh: 他信任我能在他先攀爬时保护他的安全，尽管我几乎不知道自己在做什么。

sentences.en: Where next, I say, euphoric at having overcome fear.
sentences.zh: “接下来去哪？”我说，克服恐惧后的我感到欣喜若狂。

sentences.en: And now, he's looking at me with something like pride and delight in my delight and warm affection and deep recognition of me that has nothing to do with words.
sentences.zh: 现在，他看着我，眼神中带着一种自豪和喜悦，那是对我快乐的共鸣，是一种温暖的爱意和深切的认同，无需言语。

sentences.en: And I think, so this is what love is.
sentences.zh: 我想，原来这就是爱。

sentences.en: Wow, I mean, I really feel like you were, I don't want to take you too far, like you were so in the world of that essay.
sentences.zh: 哇，我是说，我真的觉得你当时，我不想让你陷得太深，你完全沉浸在那篇文章的世界里了。

sentences.en: What are your immediate reactions to having read that piece?
sentences.zh: 读完那篇文章，你有什么直接的反应？

sentences.en: Um, there are kind of four things that really struck me about that essay.
sentences.zh: 嗯，那篇文章有四点真的打动了我。

sentences.en: And the first is how much we resist the thing that we want moSt.
sentences.zh: 第一点是，我们是多么抗拒自己最想要的东西。

sentences.en: You know, as she was going through the details of how hard she was making it to meet somebody.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当她详细描述自己是如何阻碍自己去遇见某人时。

sentences.en: The picture, the, yeah, the putting her location, that where she, yeah.
sentences.zh: 那张照片，那个，是的，还有她设置的定位，她所在的地方，是的。

sentences.en: All of it.
sentences.zh: 所有这些。

sentences.en: And she used the word ambivalence.
sentences.zh: 她用了“矛盾”这个词。

sentences.en: And it's very hard to get what you want in life and in love if you're ambivalent about whether or not you're going to get it.
sentences.zh: 如果你对是否能得到某样东西感到矛盾，那么在生活和爱情中，你很难得到它。

sentences.en: Huh.
sentences.zh: 哈。

sentences.en: You mean like we must believe we will?
sentences.zh: 你是说我们必须相信自己能得到？

sentences.en: Meaning, why make it harder for yourself?
sentences.zh: 意思是，为什么要给自己增加难度呢？

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Why cross your arms and lean back and kind of say, you got to prove it to me?
sentences.zh: 为什么要交叉双臂、向后靠着说：“你得向我证明”？

sentences.en: Huh.
sentences.zh: 哈。

sentences.en: I think it's easier in life if you open your arms and lean in and you not only go for the
sentences.zh: 我觉得如果你敞开双臂、身体前倾，不仅去追求你想要的

sentences.en: things that you want, trusting in your capacity to understand who's right and who's wrong for
sentences.zh: 东西，相信自己有能力判断谁是对的人、谁是错的人，生活会更容易，

sentences.en: you, but also there is this, I believe, energetic exchange that happens when you open your arms to the world.
sentences.zh: 而且我相信，当你向世界敞开双臂时，会发生一种能量交换。

sentences.en: I believe it opens its arms back to you.
sentences.zh: 我相信世界也会向你敞开双臂。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: And so one of the things that really struck me, and I think it's very, very relatable,
sentences.zh: 所以，其中一点真的打动了我，而且我认为这非常有共鸣，

sentences.en: is that if you've been alone for a long time or if you've been through heartbreak or you had a
sentences.zh: 就是如果你已经单身很久，或者经历过心碎，或者经历过一段非常动荡的关系，

sentences.en: very turbulent relationship, it is normal and explainable and understandable to be nervous about, quote, putting yourself back out there.
sentences.zh: 那么对于“重新开始”感到紧张是正常的、可解释的，也是可以理解的。

sentences.en: Totally.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But if you really do want to meet somebody to share a life with, what option do you have?
sentences.zh: 但如果你真的想遇见某人共度余生，你还有什么选择呢？

sentences.en: I hear what you're saying.
sentences.zh: 我明白你的意思。

sentences.en: It's like the sort of half in, half out is not going to, likely will not get you what you want if you are truly looking for a connection, a partner.
sentences.zh: 就像那种半推半就的状态，如果你真的在寻找联结、寻找伴侣，那很可能无法让你如愿。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的，是的，是的。

sentences.en: Correct, because you're always going to be handing the other person power.
sentences.zh: 没错，因为你总是在把权力交给对方。

sentences.en: I'm worried about getting hurt, so I'm going to let you have all the power, and then I'm going to sit here and assess and be managing whether or not you're going to hurt me.
sentences.zh: “我担心受伤，所以我把所有权力都交给你，然后我坐在这里评估并管理你是否会伤害我。”

sentences.en: And I think there's a very different way to go about, quote, putting yourself out there and being open to somebody entering your life.
sentences.zh: 我认为，去“重新开始”并对某人进入你的生活保持开放，有完全不同的方式。

sentences.en: And this brings me to the second theme that was very strong in this essay, which is about control.
sentences.zh: 这就引出了这篇文章中非常强烈的主题，即关于控制。

sentences.en: I think in today's world, when it comes to love, there is so much power that people give to the apps.
sentences.zh: 我认为在当今世界，谈到爱情，人们把太多的权力交给了约会软件。

sentences.en: And there's a huge narrative about how creepy and scummy people are on the apps.
sentences.zh: 而且关于约会软件上的人有多恶心、多卑劣，有太多的负面叙事。

sentences.en: And here's what I'm here to tell you.
sentences.zh: 我想告诉你的是。

sentences.en: Tell me, because I need help.
sentences.zh: 请告诉我，因为我需要帮助。

sentences.en: You can't just blame the apps.
sentences.zh: 你不能只怪约会软件。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的，是的，是的。

sentences.en: The apps are a way to meet people.
sentences.zh: 约会软件只是遇见人的一种方式。

sentences.en: And the purpose of dating is not to find the one.
sentences.zh: 约会的目的不是为了找到“那个人”。

sentences.en: The purpose of dating is for you to learn more about yourself, what you like, what you don't like, what your biases are, what they're not.
sentences.zh: 约会的目的是让你更了解自己，了解你喜欢什么、不喜欢什么，你的偏见是什么，什么不是。

sentences.en: And one of the things that happens is people kind of put their toe in the water by getting on the apps.
sentences.zh: 人们通过使用约会软件来试水，这就会发生一种情况：

sentences.en: And then they're super frustrated because the people that they're introduced to on the apps, they don't like.
sentences.zh: 他们会感到非常沮丧，因为他们通过软件认识的人，他们并不喜欢。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But if you look at what's in your control, what's in your control is how you go through your day.
sentences.zh: 但如果你看看什么是你能控制的，你能控制的是你如何度过每一天。

sentences.en: If you really want to meet somebody, when you stand in a line, are you talking to people?
sentences.zh: 如果你真的想遇见某人，当你排队时，你会和人交谈吗？

sentences.en: When you go out with your friends to a restaurant or a bar, are you waiting for other people to approach you as if it's an app?
sentences.zh: 当你和朋友去餐厅或酒吧时，你是在等着别人来接近你，就像在用约会软件一样吗？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Or are you seeing somebody who's interesting and you're talking to them?
sentences.zh: 还是说你看到有趣的人就会主动去和他们交谈？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: There are people all over the place.
sentences.zh: 到处都是人。

sentences.en: There are people all around you.
sentences.zh: 你周围到处都是人。

sentences.en: There are people that your colleagues know.
sentences.zh: 你同事认识的人里也有。

sentences.en: But if you're not open to meeting somebody and trusting in your ability to know when to lean
sentences.zh: 但如果你不敞开心扉去遇见某人，也不相信自己有能力知道何时该前倾

sentences.en: in and when to lean out, then you're going to narrow the field by only going on the apps
sentences.zh: 何时该进，何时该退，然后你又通过只在交友软件上找人来缩小范围，

sentences.en: and then being upset by the fact that of the 50 people you get matched with, only two people are interesting.
sentences.zh: 接着又因为匹配到的50个人里只有两个让你感兴趣而感到沮丧。

sentences.en: Well, guess what?
sentences.zh: 嗯，你猜怎么着？

sentences.en: You were matched with 50 to meet the two.
sentences.zh: 你匹配了50个人，就是为了遇见那两个。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: I know you're kind of doing like the universal you, but I do genuinely feel like you're saying you as in Anna, and I need to hear this.
sentences.zh: 我知道你说的“你”是指大众，但我真的觉得你是在说我，安娜，我需要听听这些。

sentences.en: So that is really, it's good to, it's good to know.
sentences.zh: 所以这真的，这很好，很高兴能知道这些。

sentences.en: I mean, yeah, it's, it's really interesting.
sentences.zh: 我是说，是的，这真的很有意思。

sentences.en: It's like the, the things very often we hear, you know, anecdotally, whatever, with my friends,
sentences.zh: 就像我们经常听到的那些事，你知道，道听途说的也好，别的什么也好，我朋友们那边，

sentences.en: we certainly hear, you know, when we've had people on the show who are on apps, like, yeah, this lack of control.
sentences.zh: 我们确实听过，你知道，当我们在节目里请到那些用交友软件的人时，他们会说，没错，这种缺乏掌控感。

sentences.en: It's like this app is feeding me people that I don't like.
sentences.zh: 就像这个软件一直在给我推送我不喜欢的人。

sentences.en: Hold on a second.
sentences.zh: 等一下。

sentences.en: Here's the thing though, Anna.
sentences.zh: 但问题在于，安娜。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Have you looked at your filters?
sentences.zh: 你检查过你的筛选条件了吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 检查过。

sentences.en: Like everybody loves to sit back and complain about the apps feeding you people, but have you actually looked at your filters?
sentences.zh: 就像每个人都喜欢坐着抱怨软件推送的人不对，但你真的看过你的筛选条件吗？

sentences.en: Because I guarantee you, you Frankensteined a person that doesn't exiSt.
sentences.zh: 因为我敢保证，你拼凑出了一个根本不存在的人。

sentences.en: You're like, okay, I'll take it this tall, only within five miles.
sentences.zh: 你就像是，好吧，我要这个身高的，只能在五英里以内的。

sentences.en: They got to make this kind of money.
sentences.zh: 他们得赚多少多少钱。

sentences.en: They can't possibly smoke.
sentences.zh: 他们绝对不能抽烟。

sentences.en: They have to be like this and that and the other thing.
sentences.zh: 他们必须得是这样那样，还有别的什么要求。

sentences.en: And you have so narrowed to the same biased point of view, the exact person that doesn't exist that everybody else is looking for.
sentences.zh: 你把范围缩小到了一个带有偏见的死胡同里，去寻找那个每个人都在找的、根本不存在的人。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: If you were to get rid of the filters, any height.
sentences.zh: 如果你能去掉这些筛选条件，不限身高。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: That's a tough one.
sentences.zh: 这很难。

sentences.en: 25 miles away, 50 miles away.
sentences.zh: 25英里外，50英里外。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: If the love of your life that was going to build an incredible life with you live 50 miles away, wouldn't you want to meet him?
sentences.zh: 如果那个能和你共建美好生活的真命天子住在50英里外，你难道不想遇见他吗？

sentences.en: Definitely.
sentences.zh: 当然想。

sentences.en: I mean, this is what the essay, the essay is like, these people were what, you know, like hundreds of miles away, although this person that she ultimately did match with
sentences.zh: 我是说，这就是那篇文章的主旨，文章里说，这些人，你知道，离得有几百英里远，尽管她最终匹配到的那个人，

sentences.en: or started talking to, the climber, did live closer to home.
sentences.zh: 或者说开始交谈的那个人，那个登山者，其实住得离家更近。

sentences.en: But even what you're saying, like she saw his profile.
sentences.zh: 但即使按你说的，她看到了他的个人资料。

sentences.en: She saw that he was good at chopping wood.
sentences.zh: 她看到他很擅长劈柴。

sentences.en: That was awesome.
sentences.zh: 那太棒了。

sentences.en: But she's terrified of heights.
sentences.zh: 但她恐高。

sentences.en: So it's like the climbing aspect almost disqualified him.
sentences.zh: 所以就像是登山这个方面差点让他出局了。

sentences.en: And the essay does a really interesting thing where it jumps.
sentences.zh: 而且这篇文章做了一件很有趣的事，它跳跃了。

sentences.en: Hold on.
sentences.zh: 等一下。

sentences.en: Did it disqualify him?
sentences.zh: 是他出局了吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Or did she disqualify herself?
sentences.zh: 还是她让自己出局了？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Boom.
sentences.zh: 砰。

sentences.en: See, that's the other thing that I think that is problematic is that we disqualify ourselves because we are afraid that somebody's not going to choose us.
sentences.zh: 看，我认为另一个有问题的地方在于，我们因为害怕别人不会选择我们，就先把自己淘汰了。

sentences.en: I mean, the beautiful thing about love is you get to choose who and how you love.
sentences.zh: 我是说，爱情的美妙之处在于，你可以选择去爱谁，以及如何去爱。

sentences.en: And the process of finding somebody not to date, because you're not put on this earth to be somebody's wife or husband.
sentences.zh: 寻找伴侣的过程不是为了去约会，因为你来到这个世上不是为了做谁的妻子或丈夫。

sentences.en: You have a big, you have a big, beautiful life, and the person that you're going to meet is somebody that you are going to share that life with.
sentences.zh: 你拥有一个宏大而美好的人生，而你即将遇见的那个人，是你将要与之分享这份人生的人。

sentences.en: So you got to be choosy.
sentences.zh: 所以你得挑剔一点。

sentences.en: The process of finding the right person for you is a process of saying no.
sentences.zh: 寻找对的人的过程，就是一个不断说“不”的过程。

sentences.en: And the wider the net that you put out, the faster you're going to have no's to get to a yes.
sentences.zh: 你撒的网越广，你就越快能通过排除掉那些“不”，从而找到那个“是”。

sentences.en: And the thing that is really sad about love is that we have such a vision for what it should be that we close off the possibility of what it could be.
sentences.zh: 关于爱情最可悲的一点是，我们对它应该是什么样子有着太固执的设想，以至于我们关闭了它可能成为什么样子的可能性。

sentences.en: And the other piece that I'll say about this is that, you know, I think the thing that we chase is that sizzle and that spark and that love at first sight.
sentences.zh: 关于这一点，我还要说的是，你知道，我认为我们所追逐的往往是那种心动、火花和一见钟情。

sentences.en: I personally prefer the slow burn.
sentences.zh: 我个人更喜欢细水长流。

sentences.en: I say to my daughters and my son all the time, the person that is your person, and I don't believe there's only one person for you.
sentences.zh: 我总是对我的女儿和儿子说，那个属于你的人——我不相信这世上只有一个属于你的人，

sentences.en: I think there's lots of people that can be your person.
sentences.zh: 我认为有很多人都可以成为你的人。

sentences.en: They need to feel like home base.
sentences.zh: 他们需要让你感到像回到家一样。

sentences.en: You know, life is hard enough.
sentences.zh: 你知道，生活已经够难了。

sentences.en: Looks fade.
sentences.zh: 容貌会衰老。

sentences.en: People get fat.
sentences.zh: 人会发胖。

sentences.en: People get out of shape.
sentences.zh: 人会走形。

sentences.en: People get cancer.
sentences.zh: 人会得癌症。

sentences.en: People lose their hair.
sentences.zh: 人会脱发。

sentences.en: All kinds of things are going to happen to you.
sentences.zh: 各种各样的事情都会发生在你身上。

sentences.en: But the one thing that won't change if you're with the right person is that when you get home at the end of the day and you walk in the door,
sentences.zh: 但如果你和对的人在一起，有一件事是不会变的，那就是当你一天结束回到家，走进门时，

sentences.en: being with them feels like an exhale.
sentences.zh: 和他们在一起的感觉就像长舒了一口气。

sentences.en: That's what you're looking for.
sentences.zh: 这就是你在寻找的东西。

sentences.en: And what I love about this story is that she almost opted out of this because she was saying, I can't be with somebody who climbs.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢这个故事的一点是，她差点就因为说“我不能和一个登山的人在一起”而错过了这段缘分。

sentences.en: Because she said yes and met him,
sentences.zh: 因为她说了“是”并见了他，

sentences.en: look at what he has opened up in terms of what's possible for her and what she's learning about herself and how her life is changing because this is a person who does something that she never thought she could do.
sentences.zh: 看看他为她打开了怎样的新世界，让她看到了各种可能性，让她了解了自己，让她的生活发生了怎样的改变，因为这是一个做着她从未想过自己能做之事的人。

sentences.en: And so, you know, my main thing that I would say if you're somebody who's putting yourself back out there is it is normal to be nervous.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，如果你是一个正准备重新开始寻找伴侣的人，我想说的是，感到紧张是很正常的。

sentences.en: It is normal to see all of the frogs before you, like, find somebody who's a fit.
sentences.zh: 在找到合适的人之前，经历各种各样的“青蛙”也是正常的。

sentences.en: It's all about saying no and opening yourself up to meeting all different kinds of people.
sentences.zh: 关键在于学会说“不”，并敞开心扉去接触各种各样的人。

sentences.en: And you need to keep saying to yourself, what if it works out?
sentences.zh: 你需要不断对自己说：万一成了呢？

sentences.en: That's an act of trust, by the way.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，这是一种信任的行为。

sentences.en: And when you recognize you can trust yourself, then you're not in danger.
sentences.zh: 当你意识到你可以信任自己时，你就不会处于危险之中。

sentences.en: You're not going to get hurt because you know that your control and the power is in you and your capacity to recognize situations that are worth continuing and situations that are worth ending.
sentences.zh: 你不会受到伤害，因为你知道掌控权和力量都在你手中，在于你有能力识别哪些情况值得继续，哪些情况值得结束。

sentences.en: And the final thing is, in order to be loved and to have love in your life, you have to allow love in.
sentences.zh: 最后一点是，为了被爱并在生活中拥有爱，你必须允许爱进入你的生命。

sentences.en: And that's, to me, what the climbing story represents.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，这就是那个登山故事所代表的含义。

sentences.en: She is roped up.
sentences.zh: 她系着绳索。

sentences.en: She is safe.
sentences.zh: 她是安全的。

sentences.en: She is panicking.
sentences.zh: 她在恐慌。

sentences.en: She's bitching at the guy who's telling her that she's safe, resisting the support and love that's there.
sentences.zh: 她在冲那个告诉她“你是安全的”的人发火，抗拒着那份本就在身边的支持与爱。

sentences.en: And we all do that.
sentences.zh: 我们都会那样做。

sentences.en: How often do you cross your arms?
sentences.zh: 你多久会交叉双臂一次？

sentences.en: How often do you hold up the sword?
sentences.zh: 你多久会举起剑一次？

sentences.en: How often do you block it?
sentences.zh: 你多久会阻挡它一次？

sentences.en: Learning how to allow it in will create more love in your life.
sentences.zh: 学会如何让爱进入，会为你的生活创造更多的爱。

sentences.en: I guess I wonder, like, is there an example from your life?
sentences.zh: 我其实想问，你生活中有什么例子吗？

sentences.en: You know, we're sort of locating this within the world of the essay, but to move it to your experience, like,
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们现在是在文章的语境下讨论，但如果转到你的经历，比如，

sentences.en: can you share a moment from a relationship where you had this kind of experience where you had to trust yourself?
sentences.zh: 你能分享一段你在一段关系中经历过这种时刻，不得不信任自己的故事吗？

sentences.en: Can you share something that has happened to you like this?
sentences.zh: 你能分享一些发生在你身上的类似事情吗？

sentences.en: Well, I found myself in that exact position because my husband, Chris, is a huge outdoorsman.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我发现自己就处于那种境地，因为我丈夫克里斯是个超级户外运动爱好者。

sentences.en: And even though I grew up in western Michigan and we camped and we fished and did lots of fun things, like, Chris did it on a whole different level.
sentences.zh: 尽管我在密歇根州西部长大，我们也会露营、钓鱼，做很多有趣的事，但克里斯的级别完全不同。

sentences.en: I mean, he's, like, living in the Rocky Mountains and building igloos and all.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他就像是住在落基山脉里，盖冰屋什么的。

sentences.en: So I have found myself in multiple situations with him.
sentences.zh: 所以我发现自己和他在一起时，经常处于各种境地。

sentences.en: Whether it's salmon fishing in Alaska and while he's casting for the King's Salmon Run,
sentences.zh: 比如在阿拉斯加钓鲑鱼，当他在为帝王鲑洄游抛竿时，

sentences.en: I'm holding a freaking rifle that I barely know how to use because the grizzlies are coming down to feed.
sentences.zh: 我手里拿着一把我几乎不会用的破步枪，因为灰熊正下来觅食。

sentences.en: And I'm thinking, what on earth have I gotten myself into?
sentences.zh: 我在想，我到底把自己卷进了什么鬼地方？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And so in any great relationship, I hope you find yourself in these moments where you're doing something you never thought possible,
sentences.zh: 所以在任何伟大的关系中，我希望你都能发现自己处于这些时刻，做着你从未想过可能做到的事，

sentences.en: where you are trying things that you've never done before, because that's the beauty of being with somebody.
sentences.zh: 尝试着你从未做过的事，因为这就是与某人在一起的美妙之处。

sentences.en: How did you learn to do that?
sentences.zh: 你是怎么学会这样做的？

sentences.en: Was there a moment like this woman on the side of the mountain or was it more gradual for you?
sentences.zh: 是有过像这个女人在山壁上那样的时刻，还是对你来说更循序渐进？

sentences.en: I think it was 1,000% gradual because I handed it over to everybody else.
sentences.zh: 我觉得是1000%循序渐进的，因为我把掌控权交给了别人。

sentences.en: Oh, you're going to break my truSt.
sentences.zh: 哦，你要破坏我的信任。

sentences.en: Now you've got to earn my trust back.
sentences.zh: 现在你得重新赢回我的信任。

sentences.en: And all of the kind of pretending in a relationship so that the person likes you.
sentences.zh: 还有在一段关系中为了让对方喜欢你而进行的各种伪装。

sentences.en: I was the kind of person that when I was in a relationship, I literally became like a human anemone that would change into the environment that I was in.
sentences.zh: 我以前就是那种人，在一段关系中，我简直变成了一只人类海葵，会根据所处的环境改变自己。

sentences.en: If you liked rock music, I liked rock music.
sentences.zh: 如果你喜欢摇滚乐，我就喜欢摇滚乐。

sentences.en: Country, oh, I'm a country girl.
sentences.zh: 乡村音乐？哦，我是个乡村女孩。

sentences.en: Oh, Grateful Dead, deadhead all the way.
sentences.zh: 哦，感恩而死乐队？我是死忠粉。

sentences.en: Oh, you like rap?
sentences.zh: 哦，你喜欢说唱？

sentences.en: Me too.
sentences.zh: 我也喜欢。

sentences.en: Ska, oh, I'm there.
sentences.zh: 斯卡曲风？哦，我也在行。

sentences.en: Yes, let's go.
sentences.zh: 是的，走吧。

sentences.en: And so I feel that for me, I wish I had had the let them theory a long time ago,
sentences.zh: 所以我感觉，对于我来说，我真希望很久以前就懂“让他们做自己”的理论，

sentences.en: because one of the most important things in dating and love is being very clear that the other person is who they are.
sentences.zh: 因为在约会和爱情中，最重要的事情之一就是非常清楚对方就是他们自己。

sentences.en: And their behavior tells you exactly how they feel about you and whether or not you're a priority.
sentences.zh: 他们的行为会准确地告诉你他们对你的感觉，以及你是否是他们的优先事项。

sentences.en: And it would have helped me very clearly to let people be who they are, let people like me or not like me, and not cross that line and try to just be near somebody.
sentences.zh: 如果我能早点明白，就能很清楚地让人们做他们自己，让人们喜欢我或不喜欢我，而不是越界去试图仅仅为了靠近某人而改变。

sentences.en: And if I hang out with them all the time, yes, or be in a relationship with the fantasy instead of recognizing the reality that I'm in.
sentences.zh: 如果我一直和他们待在一起，或者沉浸在幻想的关系中，而不是认清我所处的现实，那该多好。

sentences.en: You know, when I listen to you talk about this essay about your own experience, about the let them theory, I feel so like reared up to go, to trust myself, to let them, to let me.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当我听你谈论这篇文章，谈论你自己的经历，谈论“让他们做自己”的理论时，我感觉自己充满了动力，去信任自己，让他们做自己，让我做自己。

sentences.en: But I also know that, like, when I get out of this room and I unsilence my phone and all the notifications pour in, whatever,
sentences.zh: 但我同时也知道，当我走出这个房间，打开手机，各种通知涌进来的时候，不管怎样，

sentences.en: I'm gonna still feel that deep impulse to control or to mold or to, you know, it's gonna be tough.
sentences.zh: 我还是会感到那种想要控制或塑造对方的深层冲动，你知道，这会很难。

sentences.en: Do you ever find it difficult to follow your own advice?
sentences.zh: 你有没有发现遵循自己的建议很难？

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: You do?
sentences.zh: 真的吗？

sentences.en: Always.
sentences.zh: 总是这样。

sentences.en: Oh, my God.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: It's like, I invented a trick for getting out of bed.
sentences.zh: 就像，我发明了一个起床的诀窍。

sentences.en: I have trouble getting out of bed.
sentences.zh: 我起床也很困难。

sentences.en: Like, I, just because I've found shortcuts that help me doesn't mean I'm not human.
sentences.zh: 就像，我找到了能帮到我的捷径，并不代表我就不是凡人了。

sentences.en: And I think the biggest mistake and the most dangerous place to be in when you're dating is, you know,
sentences.zh: 而且我认为在约会时，最大的错误和最危险的处境是，你知道，

sentences.en: when you're first in it and you're putting yourself out there and you're seeing a million people and you're like, okay, got to say a lot of no's to get to the yes.
sentences.zh: 当你刚开始，正把自己推向市场，见了一百万人，你会想，好吧，得说很多个“不”才能找到那个“是”。

sentences.en: No, no, no, no, no, no, no.
sentences.zh: 不，不，不，不，不，不，不。

sentences.en: Okay, yes.
sentences.zh: 好吧，是。

sentences.en: When you have a few yeses and you're fooling around and then all of a sudden you realize, you know, this isn't just a yes, this is a hell yes.
sentences.zh: 当你有了几个“是”，并且在交往时，突然意识到，你知道，这不仅仅是一个“是”，这是一个“绝对是”。

sentences.en: That's when things get scary because now you want it to go from something casual to something that is more permanent and more solid and that makes you feel a little more in control.
sentences.zh: 那时候事情就变得可怕了，因为现在你想要从随意的关系变成更永久、更稳固的关系，这让你感觉稍微更有掌控感一点。

sentences.en: And this is the first moment where you have to trust yourself because the second you get to the point where you know you want more, you want to put a label on it,
sentences.zh: 这是你必须信任自己的第一个时刻，因为当你意识到你想要更多，你想要给这段关系贴上标签的那一刻，

sentences.en: you want to be exclusive, you want to move in together, you want to get engaged, you want to have kids, you want to get married.
sentences.zh: 你想要排他，想要同居，想要订婚，想要孩子，想要结婚。

sentences.en: Whatever that more is, you owe it to yourself to actually ask for it.
sentences.zh: 无论那个“更多”是什么，你都有义务对自己诚实，勇敢地提出来。

sentences.en: And there's an important way to ask for this.
sentences.zh: 而且提出来的方式很重要。

sentences.en: You go to the person that you've been a yes with and you basically say, I really think you're amazing.
sentences.zh: 你去找那个你已经确认过是“是”的人，基本上说，我觉得你真的很棒。

sentences.en: I love hanging out with you.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢和你在一起。

sentences.en: I would hang out with you all the time.
sentences.zh: 我愿意一直和你在一起。

sentences.en: And I've gotten to the point where I just know myself.
sentences.zh: 我已经到了一个了解自己的阶段。

sentences.en: I really want to be exclusive or I want to be your girlfriend or I'm ready to get engaged or I need to know if you want to have kids too.
sentences.zh: 我真的很想确定排他关系，或者我想做你的女朋友，或者我已经准备好订婚了，或者我需要知道你是否也想要孩子。

sentences.en: And you may not want these things, but I just know myself.
sentences.zh: 你可能不想要这些，但我只是了解我自己。

sentences.en: Because if you don't want the same thing that I want, then I don't want to spend any more time and energy in this.
sentences.zh: 因为如果你想要的和我想要的不一样，那我就不想再在这上面浪费时间和精力了。

sentences.en: That's so interesting.
sentences.zh: 那太有意思了。

sentences.en: It's almost like let me is first in this instance and then let them is next.
sentences.zh: 这几乎就像是说，在这种情况下，先考虑“我”，然后再考虑“他们”。

sentences.en: Yes, because you're not saying you've been leading me on and we need to get that.
sentences.zh: 没错，因为你并不是在说你一直在吊着我，我们需要明确这一点。

sentences.en: You're not putting that.
sentences.zh: 你不是在表达那个意思。

sentences.en: It's not about them.
sentences.zh: 这与他们无关。

sentences.en: You respect your own time and energy.
sentences.zh: 你要尊重自己的时间和精力。

sentences.en: That's where the trust and the control comes in is you knowing when I get to the point where I need to be exclusive or it needs to go to the next thing.
sentences.zh: 这就是信任和掌控力的体现，你要知道什么时候该进入排他性关系，或者什么时候该进入下一个阶段。

sentences.en: It is a waste of time to spend time with somebody who doesn't want that.
sentences.zh: 把时间花在不想那样做的人身上，纯属浪费时间。

sentences.en: Mel, I'll really close with this.
sentences.zh: 梅尔，我最后想说这一点。

sentences.en: What is the last?
sentences.zh: 最后一点是什么？

sentences.en: Well, I want to ask you one thing.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想问你一件事。

sentences.en: Please.
sentences.zh: 请说。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Let me ask you this.
sentences.zh: 让我问你这个。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: I'm scared.
sentences.zh: 我很害怕。

sentences.en: I'm ready.
sentences.zh: 我准备好了。

sentences.en: No, if you knew the love of your life was literally nine months away, like the person that you're going to build a beautiful life with,
sentences.zh: 不，如果你知道你的一生挚爱就在九个月后出现，就是那个你要与他共建美好生活的人，

sentences.en: the person that you're going to walk in the door at the end of the day and just exhale.
sentences.zh: 那个让你在一天结束时推门而入，就能长舒一口气的人。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: If you knew you were going to bump into that person nine months from now, how would you spend the next nine months?
sentences.zh: 如果你知道九个月后会遇见那个人，你会如何度过接下来的九个月？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Are you really asking me that?
sentences.zh: 你真的在问我这个问题吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, it's funny.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这很有趣。

sentences.en: My therapist asked me literally the exact same question.
sentences.zh: 我的治疗师也问过我完全相同的问题。

sentences.en: I think I would just feel so much lighter.
sentences.zh: 我想我会感到轻松得多。

sentences.en: Like there would be such a pressure off.
sentences.zh: 就像卸下了巨大的压力一样。

sentences.en: And I'm really trying to channel that, even though no one can guarantee me that, which is tough.
sentences.zh: 我真的在努力引导这种心态，尽管没有人能向我保证什么，这很难。

sentences.en: Who says?
sentences.zh: 谁说的？

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: We can't guarantee that.
sentences.zh: 我们无法保证这一点。

sentences.en: Who says they can't guarantee that?
sentences.zh: 谁说他们不能保证这一点？

sentences.en: Really?
sentences.zh: 真的吗？

sentences.en: Why not?
sentences.zh: 为什么不能？

sentences.en: Why not?
sentences.zh: 为什么不能？

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: Because will that happen in nine months?
sentences.zh: 因为那会在九个月内发生吗？

sentences.en: Why do you like, like, this is where the faith comes in.
sentences.zh: 为什么你……这就是信念发挥作用的地方。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: That if I were to open up my arms and I were to trust myself and I were to go about my life in a way that makes me happy and I feel like myself and I'm not trying to jam a square peg into a round hole and I'm not gripped about when this is happening and everything else,
sentences.zh: 如果我敞开双臂，信任自己，以一种让我快乐、让我感觉真实的方式生活，不再试图削足适履，也不再纠结于这一切何时发生，

sentences.en: but I just open up my arms and I believe and I go about my life.
sentences.zh: 而是敞开双臂，保持信念，继续我的生活。

sentences.en: You are now shifting the energy and you're focusing on what you can control and that shift alone will actually pull in the right person.
sentences.zh: 你现在正在转变能量，专注于你能控制的事情，而仅仅是这种转变，实际上就会吸引对的人来到你身边。

sentences.en: You're right.
sentences.zh: 你说得对。

sentences.en: Opening the arms, as you said, to the world.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，向世界敞开双臂。

sentences.en: Listen, Mel, we can circle back in nine months and I'll let you know if I've found that person.
sentences.zh: 听着，梅尔，九个月后我们可以再聊聊，我会告诉你我是否找到了那个人。

sentences.en: Oh, I'm going to be right.
sentences.zh: 哦，我会是对的。

sentences.en: I know it.
sentences.zh: 我知道。

sentences.en: I honestly believe you, which is exciting for me.
sentences.zh: 我真心相信你，这让我感到很兴奋。

sentences.en: My God.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: Mel Robbins, thank you so much for this conversation today.
sentences.zh: 梅尔·罗宾斯，非常感谢你今天的谈话。

sentences.en: Well, thank you.
sentences.zh: 嗯，谢谢你。

sentences.en: Oh, and thank you for being open to everything we talked about.
sentences.zh: 哦，也谢谢你对我们谈论的一切持开放态度。

sentences.en: I really want that for you.
sentences.zh: 我真心希望你能得到这一切。

sentences.en: You deserve that.
sentences.zh: 你值得拥有。

sentences.en: Thank you, Mel.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，梅尔。
